name: Eiffage SA
reason: Adj EPS rose from EUR 3.33 (2015) to EUR 11.01 (2025), but it has been flat at about EUR 11 since 2023; 10y average ROIC is only 4.2% and net debt is 2.4x EBITDA; profits lean on APRR toll-road concessions that face French concession-tax policy risk and expiry in the mid-2030s, so earnings cannot be forecast 10 years out.

name: Inmocemento SA
reason: 2024 spin-off with only 2 years of history (GAAP EPS EUR 0.33 to EUR 0.76); earnings come from Spanish cement and property development, a construction/real-estate-cycle business with no specialness, and no consensus is available.

name: Signify NV
reason: Revenue has fallen 2.6%/yr over 10 years as conventional lighting declines; adj EPS of EUR 2.40 in 2025 is below the EUR 4.18 peak in 2022, consensus FY1 is -35%, and 10y average ROIC is 7.6%, so it is a cheap but ordinary commoditising hardware maker.

name: Renewables Infrastructure Group Ltd
reason: Renewables investment trust whose earnings are fair-value marks driven by power prices and discount rates (EBIT margin swings from +396% to -103%, consensus FY1 -524%); share count has grown 15.5%/yr, so earnings are set by commodity and rate cycles.

name: Criteo SA
reason: Adtech intermediary: adj EPS of USD 4.62 is at its 10y high, EBIT margin is at its 100th percentile (11.4% vs a 6.9% average), and consensus FY1 is -24%; it faces credible 5-year threats from browser/privacy changes and the loss of a large retail-media client, and the adj-vs-GAAP gap is 474%.

name: Havas NV
reason: Ad agency spun out of Vivendi in Dec-2024 with a short record (GAAP EPS EUR 4.01 in 2022 to EUR 1.91 in 2025); 10y average ROIC is 8.2%, consensus growth is about 8%, and it faces a credible AI threat to labour-based agency billing, so there is no specialness.

name: Endeavour Mining Plc
reason: West African gold miner whose earnings are set by the gold price: adj EPS of USD 3.23 is at its 10y high and EBIT margin is at its 100th percentile (44% vs a 23% average); shares have grown 19%/yr and there is Sahel political risk.

name: CTT - Correios de Portugal SA
reason: Declining postal mail plus a parcels business and a small bank (Banco CTT); adj EPS was EUR 0.52 in 2015 and only EUR 0.48 in 2023, EBIT margin fell from 14.4% to 7.2%, and the banking mix and regulated universal-service obligation make it hard to forecast.

name: Valeo SE
reason: Cyclical auto supplier: adj EPS fell from EUR 4.37 (2017) to EUR 0.81 (2025), a -12.5% 10y CAGR, with a 3.3% average EBIT margin and 3.9% ROIC; there is no durable moat and the EV transition is a technology threat.

name: Eurazeo SE
reason: Private-equity and asset-management holding company whose earnings are set by capital-markets valuations and exits: adj EPS swung from EUR 16.22 (2021) to EUR -5.87 (2025) and 10y FCF conversion is -0.32.

name: Semapa SGPS SA
reason: Holding company for pulp and paper (Navigator) plus cement, where earnings follow pulp prices: adj EPS has fallen from EUR 3.69 (2022) to EUR 1.93 (2025), consensus FY2 is -69%, and net debt is 3.6x EBITDA.

name: TORM Plc
reason: Product tanker owner whose earnings are set by spot freight rates: USD adj EPS went from -0.54 (2021) to 6.87 (2023) to 2.91 (2025), with no year of 7%+ growth on a stable base and consensus FY2/FY3 of -27% and -43%.

name: Fresenius Medical Care AG
reason: Dialysis provider earning about 70% in the US under government reimbursement; adj EPS in reporting currency was EUR 4.28 in 2025 against EUR 4.52 in 2019 (3.0% 10y CAGR), EBIT margin fell from 14.7% to 9.6%, and US payer policy plus GLP-1/kidney-drug patient-volume risk make it unforecastable.

name: OPmobility SE
reason: Cyclical auto-parts maker controlled by the Burelle family: adj EPS fell from EUR 3.32 (2018) to EUR 1.28 (2025) and EBIT margin from 8.4% to 4.2%, with 6.8% ROIC; the EV transition adds threat to its fuel-system business.

name: Electricite de Strasbourg SA
reason: About 89%-owned by EDF (French state): GAAP EPS jumped from EUR 7.66 (2022) to EUR 22.04 (2025) on post-crisis power prices, with EBIT margin at its 100th percentile (11.9% vs a 5.4% average); this is a regulated, commodity-price-peak utility with no consensus coverage.

name: Carrefour SA
reason: Low-margin grocer: adj EPS went from EUR 1.54 (2015) to EUR 1.60 (2025), a 0.4% 10y CAGR, with a 2.6% EBIT margin, 2.5% average ROIC and net debt of 3.2x; it is cheap but ordinary, with Brazil FX translation risk and a 54% adj-vs-GAAP gap.

name: Nexi SpA
reason: Merchant acquirer built by debt-funded acquisitions (SIA, Nets; acquisitions were 1.32x 10y FCF) with negative average GAAP ROE; consensus EPS growth is only 1.5-4.7%, the adj-vs-GAAP gap is 490%, and fintech competition is pressuring merchant pricing.

name: Elecnor SA
reason: Engineering and construction contractor with a 4.3% 10y average ROIC and a 5.3% average EBIT margin; GAAP EPS was negative in 2024 (EUR -1.18), consensus growth comes from a recovery off a low base, and it is family-controlled (Cantiles).

name: Mercialys SA
reason: French shopping-centre REIT: FFO per share was EUR 1.18 in 2015 and EUR 1.26 in 2025 (0.6% 10y CAGR) with net debt of 8.1x EBITDA; consensus FY2/FY3 is +1-2%, so there is no route to 7% growth.

name: Carmila SA
reason: Carrefour-anchored shopping-centre REIT: recurring EPS went from EUR 1.27 (2017) to EUR 1.81 (2025), a ~4.5%/yr gain helped by buybacks and an acquisition; net debt is 7.5x EBITDA, consensus growth is about 3%/yr, and it depends on a weak anchor tenant.
